concerns.text: The plan generates a synthetic target (yield_strength) *directly* from a known linear combination of the same composition‑only descriptors that are later used as predictors ("target yield strength drawn from a known linear model plus Gaussian noise"). This makes the validation target definitionally dependent on the predictor variables, resulting in a circular/tautological evaluation where high R² and |r| are guaranteed by construction rather than empirically demonstrated on independent real data.

The research question claims to prove real‑world predictive performance of a composition‑only model on HEAs, yet the entire pipeline is exercised on fully synthetic data. Because the synthetic data are generated from the same descriptor set, the claimed performance (R² ≥ 0.6, |r| ≥ 0.5) does not provide evidence about actual materials; the result is non‑trivial only in a simulated world and cannot be extrapolated to experimental alloys.
